10.1002_adfm.78981: Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) have emerged as transformative devices that revolutionize next‐generation electronics to bridge ionic/electronic signaling at the interface between biological and microelectronic systems. This review systematically explores fundamental breakthroughs in OECT channel material engineering and device manufacturing across micro/nanoscales for emerging bioelectronic systems, emphasizing microarchitecture design and patterning strategies that unlock advantages including enhanced transistor performance, high speed, improved mechanical durability, high‐fidelity integration, as well as biocompatibility. We first briefly introduce the device physics underpinning OECTs and state‐of‐the‐art material innovations, focusing on nanostructure‐dominated mixed ionic–electronic conduction. Subsequently, we elaborate on tailored microscale channel architectures, encompassing 1D fibers, 2D micro/nanoporous films, and 3D soft hydrogel networks to address both electronic and mechanical challenges. Furthermore, we highlight advances in scalable fabrication techniques such as printing/photolithography‐based approaches and vertical architectures for developing high‐density flexible OECT arrays. In addition, diverse bioelectronic applications are summarized, including biosensing, signal processing, implantable biointerfaces, and brain‐inspired computing, demonstrating the versatility of OECTs. The discussion concludes by outlining future directions to enhance device reliability and scalability, addressing critical challenges such as material stability and integration complexity. Through this comprehensive analysis, we provide a roadmap for advancing OECT micro/nanotechnology, inspiring future research and accelerating its adoption in bioelectronics.
10.1002_smll.202514294: Electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction reaction (CO 2 RR) is a promising approach to mitigate carbon emissions while producing value‐added fuels and chemicals. However, conventional transition‐metal catalysts suffer from limited selectivity, high overpotentials, and poor durability. Rare‐earth elements, with their unique 4f orbital configurations, variable oxidation states, and strong oxophilicity, offer distinct opportunities to overcome these limitations. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in rare‐earth‐based electrocatalysts, including single‐atom catalysts (SACs), alloys, and oxides, highlighting their ability to tailor local coordination environments, stabilize oxygenated intermediates, and facilitate multi‐electron transfer pathways. Rare‐earth‐based SACs leverage atomic dispersion to modulate electronic structures and suppress competing hydrogen evolution, while rare‐earth‐containing alloys introduce synergistic effects that disrupt conventional scaling relationships, enhancing selectivity toward desired products. Furthermore, rare‐earth oxides and mixed phases offer active oxygen vacancies and redox flexibility, thereby promoting CO 2 activation and enhancing catalyst stability. Collectively, these strategies significantly improve activity, selectivity, and durability in CO 2 RR. Despite these advances, challenges remain regarding atomic dispersion stability, conductivity, and product selectivity toward multi‐carbon species. Future research should focus on rational design guided by operando characterization, defect engineering, and machine‐learning‐assisted discovery to realize rare‐earth‐based electrocatalysts for industrially relevant, carbon‐neutral CO 2 conversion.
10.1002_smsc.202500550: In this study, the effect of the core material in hairy core–shell carriers with grafted poly(2‐(dimethylamino)ethyl methacrylate) (PDMAEMA) polymer brushes containing immobilized laccase from Trametes versicolor ( TvL ) is investigated. Conductive silver, silver‐Janus, carbon nanotubes, carbon black, and insulating silica particles were chosen as core materials. These carriers are easy to handle and store, enabling reproducible sensor fabrication with a well‐defined and high number of immobilized enzymes. Hydroquinone (HQ) detection in an aqueous system was chosen as a model for biosensor characterization. All systems demonstrated high catalytic efficiency, significantly suppressing the oxidation of HQ at the electrode surface and thereby providing selectivity. The sensitivity of the prepared sensors did not differ significantly among the carriers. However, the limit of detection was highly dependent on the overall conductivity of the carrier and its active surface area. Our main observation is that using highly conductive, high‐surface‐area carriers does not necessarily enhance sensor performance and can in fact worsen the detection limit due to the dominance of capacitive currents over faradaic ones.
10.1021_jacs.6c12759: Conventionally, the development of high-performance organic electrochemical transistor (OECT) devices heavily depends on side-chain optimization of glycolated and alkylated organic mixed ionic-electronic conducting polymers (OMIECs), which typically leads to a compromise between solubility and performance. In this study, we present a versatile design strategy employing silyl-protected side chains which can be acid-cleaved in a post-fabrication process to reveal short chains with alcohol termini, which would otherwise be unprocessable by conventional coating methods due to their insolubility. This approach decouples solubility from final device functionality, enabling solution processability during fabrication while ultimately optimizing hydrophilicity and charge transport in devices. Using PgBTTT and P100 as model polymer backbones, we demonstrate that their alcohol-functionalized analogues exhibit high μC*, excellent solvent resistance, and good electrochemical stability compared to their glycolated counterparts. Spectroelectrochemical and GIWAXS analyses reveal enhanced doping efficiency and reduced onset potentials, arising from favorable morphological reorganization upon cleavage. Overall, this work establishes alcohol functionalization as an attractive alternative to glycolation, expanding the chemical space for OMIEC device optimization and providing a platform for next-generation high-performance OECT materials.
